title: Proper closure of a generic map into a family without rational fibre curves
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $S$ a normal integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme with function field $K$ and generic point $\eta$. Let $W\to S$ be H-projective, flat and finitely presented, with nonempty connected reduced nodal geometric curve fibres and smooth geometrically integral generic fibre. Let $Q\to S$ be H-projective. Suppose that for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$, every $\Omega$-morphism $\mathbf P^1_\Omega\to Q_\Omega$ is constant. Let $u_\eta:W_\eta\to Q_\eta$ be a $K$-morphism. The relative morphism functor $T\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_T(W_T,Q_T)$ is represented by a disjoint union of quasi-projective $S$-schemes. The reduced closure $R$ of the point specified by $u_\eta$ in this morphism scheme is integral and projective birational over $S$, and its universal evaluation gives a morphism $W\times_S R\to Q\times_S R$ extending $u_\eta$. These constructions are natural under compatible isomorphisms of $S,W,Q$ preserving $u_\eta$. Thus a finite group acting on this datum acts on $R$, with equivariant evaluation. The target $Q$ need not be flat or integral. Here nodal means that the completed local ring at each singular point of a geometric fibre is $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$; a projective birational morphism is an isomorphism over a dense open.

The notions of field, integral scheme, proper morphism, finite type, geometric integrality, dimension, projectivity, finite morphism, surjectivity, function field and field extension use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension] and [def-pc-field-tower]. H-projective means admitting a closed immersion into some finite-dimensional projective space over the target. Normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains. An alteration is a proper surjective morphism of integral schemes that is finite over a dense open of its target. Group actions may be nonfaithful and may act on the ground field. Flatness, finite presentation, smoothness, geometric fibres, closed immersions, fibre products and etaleness use [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-pc-fibre-product] and [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Normalization, completion and power series use [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]; the genus of a smooth projective geometrically integral curve is [def-pc-genus].

proof.text: A field is Noetherian (its ideals are $0$ and $1$), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $S$ Noetherian. By [lem-pc-projective-base-change], $W\times_SQ\to W$ is H-projective; compose with $W\to S$ using [lem-trf-h-projective-composition] to embed it in some $\mathbf P^N_S$. Apply [lem-sfb-projective-hom-graph-parameter]: obtain $M=\coprod M_P$, the point $m:\operatorname{Spec}K\to M_P$ of $u_\eta$, open $M_P\subset H_P$ with $H_P/S$ H-projective of finite type, universal evaluation, and integral reduced closure $R\subset M_P$, separated, finite type, locally finitely presented, with $R_\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $k(R)=K$. Restrict evaluation to $R$; it extends $u_\eta$.

proof.text: Fix $A\subset K$ a DVR with fraction field $K$ and $b:T=\operatorname{Spec}A\to S$ generically the inclusion of $\eta$. A DVR is Noetherian since every ideal is principal. By [lem-trf-projective-nodal-family-geometry], $C=W_T$ retains the stated nodal curve properties; its generic fibre is $W_\eta$. By [lem-pc-projective-base-change], $X=Q_T$ is H-projective. Every geometric fibre of $X/T$ is a geometric fibre of $Q/S$, so it has the same no-rational-maps property. Apply [lem-sfb-nodal-trait-map-extension] to get $C\to X$ extending $u_\eta$. Representability from Step 1 gives $v:T\to M$ with generic restriction $m$. Its image is in $M_P$: the inverse image of this open-and-closed component contains the generic point of the connected trait $T$.

source.place: Lemma 3.13 proof, printed p.609: graph domination and contraction of rational exceptional curves. Agent-formulated no-rational-maps version; the target need not be flat, integral, or one-dimensional. Local PDF WANTED; publisher PDF read online.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-quasiprojective-point-closure-projectivity] to $M_P\subset H_P$, $m$, and $R$. Step 1 supplies all finiteness, integrality and generic-fibre hypotheses; Step 2 supplies each required DVR lift into $M_P$. Each lift factors uniquely through $R$; $R\to S$ is H-projective and an isomorphism over a dense open. With the evaluation of Step 1 this proves the geometric assertions.

proof.text: For compatible isomorphisms $\alpha_S:S\simeq S'$, $\alpha_W:W\simeq W'$ and $\alpha_Q:Q\simeq Q'$ preserving the generic morphism, conjugation sends a map $f:W_T\to Q_T$ to $\alpha_Q\circ f\circ\alpha_W^{-1}$ over the transported test scheme. The inverse conjugation makes this an isomorphism of the represented morphism functors, hence of their representing schemes by uniqueness of representing objects. It takes $m$ to $m'$, and therefore takes its topological closure with reduced induced structure to the corresponding $R'$. Universal evaluation commutes with this isomorphism because the displayed conjugation formula holds on every test scheme. This argument uses the intrinsic representing functor, so no projective embedding needs to be preserved.

source.place: 3.11, functoriality of the morphism scheme and invariance of the reduced closure

proof.text: For a finite group action on the datum, use Step 4 for each element. Write $c_g(f)=g_Q\circ f\circ g_W^{-1}$ on transported test schemes. Then $c_1=\mathrm{id}$ and $c_g(c_h(f))=(gh)_Q\circ f\circ(gh)_W^{-1}=c_{gh}(f)$. Uniqueness of representing maps gives these action laws on $R$; Step 4 gives equivariance of evaluation. The same formulas hold for semilinear isomorphisms of the ground field.
